title: Jeffrey Sachs & John Mearsheimer: Spheres of Security to Prevent World War III
summary: Sachs and Mearsheimer debate whether mutually respected great-power 'spheres of security' could prevent a US-Russia or US-China war; both blame NATO expansion for the Ukraine war.

assertions.quote: in substance what he did was provoked as John Mirshimer explained to us all in 2014
I think security competition is inevitable, as most viewers understand

verdicts.note: A structural-realist premise about international politics rather than a checkable prediction.

Clauset finds the hazard of interstate war roughly constant since 1823 despite large changes in the world, consistent with persistent competition, though he notes real mechanisms may still have lowered risk.
Braumoeller finds war persistent, but international orders can keep the peace among their members for a time, so the competition is at least partly escapable within an order.

Hanania quotes Mearsheimer and Walt on unavoidable competition (L101-114) but answers that great-power antagonism is a choice made by both sides, not 'the result of circumstances outside of human control'. Both positions are argued, not demonstrated.

assertions.quote: when it says we're 89 seconds to midnight, I do not just brush that off as empty rhetoric
But it quickly spirals into a full nuclear war between the United States and Russia because of mistakes.
walking out of the ABM treaty in 2002 and starting to put anti-bballistic missile systems, the Aegis systems in Poland and Romania.

verdicts.note: Russia treated the sites as a threat and their launchers could in principle take offensive missiles, but the few interceptors there cannot blunt Russia's large arsenal.

US intelligence confirms Moscow views US missile defences and long-range precision strike as threats to its nuclear deterrent; that is Russia's perception, not a finding that the deterrent was actually threatened.

RAND reports Russian leaders' concern about the credibility of their retaliatory forces in the face of US counterforce capability and missile defences, which shows the perceived threat but not that the ABM exit itself threatened Russia's deterrent.

assertions.quote: My point is that the Soviets and the Russians actually obeyed them.

verdicts.note: The US and NATO found Russia in violation of the INF Treaty before the US withdrew, and Russia itself suspended New START in 2023.
US intelligence says Russia has undermined arms-control agreements, suspended required New START data exchanges and deratified the CTBT, contradicting a record of compliance.

assertions.quote: My basic proposition is that the big countries, the great powers should stay out of each other's lane

verdicts.note: A policy proposal whose effect cannot be tested before it is tried.

Hanania argues that if restraint advocates pulled the US back from a militarized posture in East Asia there would be no Thucydides Trap, as when the US replaced France in Southeast Asia. This is a reasoned conjecture with no evidence that it lowers the risk of war.

assertions.quote: Putin did not incur a high reputational cost from this war

verdicts.note: Most UN members condemned the invasion, but most of the Global South declined to sanction Russia and kept trading with it.
DDIS: China, India and Türkiye buy Russian oil and China backs Russia diplomatically, but sanctions bite and Russia's influence has weakened in Central Asia and the South Caucasus.
